estimand: E[Correct if voluntary information requested] - E[Correct if not requested], within a declared Regular-trial difficulty stratum, under consistency and no other assumptions about counterfactual outcomes.
method: Sharp finite-sample binary potential-outcome bounds; A=self-selected actual information-platform landing, Y=terminal correct. No ignorability/random assignment, monotonicity or exclusion restriction imposed. For counts n11=request+correct, n10=request+wrong, n01=no request+correct, n00=no request+wrong, lower=(n11-n01-(n11+n10))/N, upper=(n11+(n01+n00)-n01)/N. These are identification bounds, not confidence intervals.
free_cue_control: Free-Cue is an automatic-delivery condition whose random interleaving the preprint describes; observed Free-Cue-vs-Regular correct rates can be reported descriptively but are not the same estimand as the effect of voluntarily purchasing a cue.
limitations: Correctness potential outcomes in the unchosen action are missing for every trial; voluntary requesting is selected by the animal.
Positive conditional accuracy difference between requesters and nonrequesters does not identify the sign of the causal effect.
Bounds do not include sampling uncertainty; population-level confidence regions would be at least as wide with appropriate uncertainty.
Quinine penalties and differential sucrose rewards imply accuracy is only one behavioral outcome, not full fitness or payoff.
A randomized Free-Cue delivery policy is different from a voluntary-request intervention. Direct visual/motor/timing effects and exclusions require independent justification.
Trial-level request/latency joins to a different experiment are invalid (cross-experiment join gate).
